summit.title: Stars between Girona and Llagostera
summit.story: The starred cooking of this coast sits inland, a short drive from the berths at Palamós. In Girona, El Celler de Can Roca opened in 1986 beside the Roca parents' family restaurant in Taialà, holds three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide and marked forty years in October 2026 with a menu of forty small dishes. In Corçà, Albert Sastregener's Bo.TiC works in a former carriage factory and took its second star in the 2021 guide. On the road from Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Els Tinars began as a roadside masia in 1978; it has held a star since 2008, and the siblings Marc and Elena Gascons run it, Marc cooking a Palamós prawn tartare that changes with the season.
summit.where: El Celler de Can Roca, Girona; Bo.TiC, Corçà; Els Tinars, Llagostera

village.title: Cove, village and cape
village.story: Away from the starred line, the coast eats in family houses and small rooms that close or slow down in winter. Casamar, on the steps above Llafranc bay, marks seventy years in 2026; Quim Casellas held a MICHELIN star there from the 2012 guide until about 2021, and the kitchen reopened on 27 March after the hotel was rebuilt. Inland at Peratallada, the Bonay family has served goose braised with turnips under the arcades of Plaça de les Voltes since 1936. At the cape end, in Cadaqués, the three chefs who later made Disfrutar opened Compartir in 2012, where every plate goes to the middle of the table.
village.where: Casamar, Llafranc; Can Bonay, Peratallada; Compartir, Cadaqués

port.title: Prawns, planxa and suquet
port.story: On this coast the fishing ports feed their own back streets, and the cooking stays close to the boat. In Palamós the red prawn is sold by falling-price auction each afternoon, and La Gamba, on Plaça de Sant Pere since the 1960s, grills it with salt a short walk from the quay. Up the coast in Roses, Rafa Cantero has run a few tables on Carrer de Sant Sebastià for more than thirty years, cooking whatever comes in on the planxa with no printed menu. In L'Estartit, opposite the Medes islands, Cal Tet is a family hotel whose ground floor is a marisqueria serving suquet and seafood rice at lunch and dinner.
port.where: La Gamba, Palamós; Rafa's, Roses; Cal Tet, L'Estartit

larder.title: Auction, salt and market
larder.story: The Costa Brava larder runs from the quay to the city. At the Llotja de Palamós the catch is sold by Dutch auction, the price falling until a buyer stops it, and the Museu de la Pesca explains the bidding on half-hour visits over the floor, EUR 3.50 in 2025. In L'Escala the Solés family has salted anchovies since 1888, in the town's oldest salting building, and opened a museum inside the factory for its 130th anniversary. Inland, Girona's covered Mercat del Lleó opened on 3 November 1944 and still trades from early morning, Monday to Saturday, with mushrooms, botifarra and Empordà cheese.
larder.where: Espai del Peix / Llotja de Palamós, Palamós; Anxoves Solés, L'Escala; Mercat del Lleó, Girona

bars.title: The cup and the cone
bars.story: Girona's old town drinks its coffee and eats its sweets in small rooms a few streets from the Onyar. La Fábrica, on Carrer de la Llebre, was opened in March 2015 by the Canadian rider Christian Meier and his wife Amber, and became the morning stop for the professional cyclists who base themselves in the city; its beans are roasted at the couple's second shop. Rocambolesc, Jordi Roca's ice-cream shop, began as the dessert trolley at El Celler de Can Roca and opened on Carrer de Santa Clara in 2012; its panet is ice cream in warm brioche, the cheapest way into the house of the three brothers.
